title: Linearity forced by many permutation translates
summary: Decide whether a polynomial whose linear translates are permutations for at least half of a finite field must be linearized.

formal_statement.body: Let $q$ be a prime power and let $F$ be a polynomial function on $\mathbb F_q$. Suppose $$\#\{c\in\mathbb F_q:x\mapsto F(x)+cx\text{ is a permutation of }\mathbb F_q\}\ge q/2.$$ Prove that $F$ must be represented by a linearized polynomial over $\mathbb F_q$, or exhibit a non-linearized polynomial function satisfying the threshold.

scope.domain: Finite-field polynomial functions with many permutation translates
assumptions: $F$ is considered as a polynomial function on $\mathbb F_q$
At least $q/2$ values $c$ make $F(x)+cx$ a permutation
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later result proves the Evans--Greene--Niederreiter implication over all finite fields or supplies a non-linearized counterexample at the $q/2$ threshold.

provenance.note: Pasalic et al. explicitly recall the Evans--Greene--Niederreiter conjecture; the 1992 Michigan Mathematical Journal paper is the cited antecedent and the 2022 TIT paper is a restatement.

citations.label: Evans--Greene--Niederreiter, linearized and permutation polynomials
citations.locator: Conjecture on permutation translates; Michigan Math. J. 39 (1992), pp. 405-413

progress.summary: Evans, Greene, and Niederreiter formulate the conjecture that at least $q/2$ permutation translates force a polynomial to be linearized.
Remark IV.2 recalls the Evans--Greene--Niederreiter conjecture that at least $q/2$ permutation translates force a polynomial to be linearized.
